title: State (BSES YPL) v. Altaf
court: Addl. Sessions Judge-05 (Electricity), East, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi
result: Convicted u/s 135 notwithstanding settlement of theft bill, deposit of amount and NOC issued by the discom; posted for sentence
statutes: Third proviso to Section 135(1) Electricity Act 2003

interpretations.interpretation: A two-core wire connected from the licensee's distribution box to unmetered premises is a clause (a) connection. 'Dishonestly' takes its s.24 IPC meaning (wrongful gain/wrongful loss).

Reverse-onus clause: proof of an artificial/unauthorised means raises a compulsory presumption of dishonest use (Neeraj Dutt) rebuttable on the prudent-man standard (Hiten P. Dalal); natural rebuttal is paid bills / lawful metered use, the s.106 Evidence Act onus lying on the consumer (Mukesh Rastogi).

Inspection power with photo-ID safeguards (60); contemporaneous report with seizure/sealing and photo/video documentation (61); prosecution only where dishonest intention evident + 24-hour police complaint + missing-seal caution (62); assessment at twice tariff up to 12 months with credit for paid units (63). Unchallenged compliance confirms regularity; the Rs. 50,979 assessment measures the theft.

citations.case: Punjab State Electricity Board v. Ashwani Kumar
citations.principle: An inspection report prepared by officers in discharge of official duty carries a presumption of regularity; onus on the consumer to rebut by cogent evidence.

citations.case: Sushil Sharma v. BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd.
citations.principle: Non-examination of an independent/public witness is no infirmity where inspecting officials are trustworthy and bear no enmity to the accused.
'Shall presume' denotes a compulsory legal presumption the court is bound to draw until the fact is disproved.

citations.case: Hiten P. Dalal v. Bratindranath Banerjee
citations.principle: Rebuttal of a statutory presumption need not be conclusive; evidence must make the defence reasonably probable to a prudent man.

citations.case: Mukesh Rastogi v. North Delhi Power Ltd.
citations.principle: Easiest rebuttal of the theft presumption is production of paid electricity bills; Section 106 Evidence Act places that onus on the consumer.

significance.point: An NOC after settlement is not immunity
significance.explanation: Payment of the settled bill and an NOC from the licensee closed the civil account only; the s.135 prosecution proceeded to conviction.
Readiness to settle rather than protest a false bill was weighed against the accused.

significance.point: A representative's presence sufficed on the facts
significance.explanation: The person at the spot identified himself as the accused's representative; unchallenged videography tied the accused, as user, to the premises.
Two IOs each proving their own documents left no exploitable gap.
No meter, distribution-box tap, unexplained load, no Genset, no paid bills — the compulsory presumption did the rest.

generic_facts.theft_mode: direct theft — two-core black wire from licensee's distribution box
generic_facts.occupant_at_inspection: per complaint accused present; per PW-3's evidence his representative present, accused the user
generic_facts.ownership_evidence: ownership documents of premises seized by IO
generic_facts.defence: bare denial/false implication; no defence evidence; settled bill + deposited + NOC issued
